palindrome:
A palindrome is a word, phrase, number, or other sequence of characters which reads the same backward as forward, ignoring spaces, punctuation, and capitalization.

Here is an example of a long palindrome:

"A man, a plan, a canal, Panama; no 'x' in Nixon."

If you want a longer one, here's another option that fits your requirement:

"Able was I ere I saw Elba. Able was I ere I saw Elba. Able was I ere I saw Elba. Able was I ere I saw Elba. Able was I ere I saw Elba. Able was I ere I saw Elba."

This palindrome repeats "Able was I ere I saw Elba" six times, making it at least 255 characters long.
